output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you very much for picking up my bag and taking the trouble to call the number in my lab manual. I am sincerely grateful that you did not throw it away, because many people would have done that. When we first spoke, you said God sent you, and I truly appreciated your kindness. I am hoping you will still show me that same kindness by helping me recover my school things.

The bag is my black Jansport, which I forgot inside a danfo travelling from Oshodi to Igando on the evening of Friday, 6 November. I came down at Ikotun. Inside are my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, my BIO 101 practical is on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10am. Without my dissecting kit and ID card, the lab attendant will not allow me to enter. As a first-year Biology student, missing this practical would create a serious problem for me.

I understand that you have spent time and possibly transport money on this, and I am not trying to disregard that. However, I honestly cannot pay ₦40,000. That amount is far beyond my means and is even more than the bag and books are worth. What I can offer is ₦10,000, which is all the allowance I have available. I am offering it willingly to cover your transport and to show my appreciation. I do not want to promise you money I do not have, so please consider accepting this in good faith. I would like us to resolve the matter reasonably and amicably.

Please choose any convenient day before Wednesday. I can meet you in the daytime at either Ikotun Roundabout or the gate of the Ikotun Police Division, whichever is easier for you. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me. I have suggested these places simply so that the handover can be open, safe and straightforward for both of us.

Kindly reply to confirm the day, time and location that suit you. Thank you once again for keeping the bag safe. I hope we can settle this peacefully and without further delay.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
